idea: Schedule the entire two-row strip as one register-allocated kernel. Reverse the reduction direction between tiles to carry A operands across the boundary, and let stores compete for issue slots as soon as individual outputs finish.
notes: Whole-strip BFS adds a store-prefix dimension to the load/MAC issue history. Register pressure counts only live results and operands, allowing a first product to overwrite a dying input. Shortlist partitions by isolated tile costs, then rerank on actual strip latency.
